artboards.role: Forno Rosso pizzeria marketing home page: site header/nav shell, hero, delivery-promise banner, featured-menu grid, brand-story section, and footer. The linked node is a single FRAME (not a CANVAS of several artboards), so the whole page is one screen; there is only one artboard to review. This story (legal static pages: Privacy Policy, Delivery Terms) is scoped to the footer's legal link row (node 6:171, specifically 6:174/6:175) and the two destination pages those links point to; the rest of the page is mapped for completeness/context only and was already the primary subject of a prior story (STORY-004, header/nav shell).

open_questions.topic: Privacy Policy and Delivery Terms pages have no Figma design at all
open_questions.detail: The only trace of these two pages in the entire frame is their nav-link labels in the footer (nodes 6:174 'Privacy Policy', 6:175 'Delivery Terms'). There is no artboard, section, or even a placeholder text block anywhere in the frame showing what either page's heading, body copy, or layout should look like. This is the central content gap for a story whose whole purpose is to ship these two pages.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Ship a minimal static content shell (H1 title + prose body, ink/Fraunces heading, muted/Geist body copy pulled from this frame's existing type ramp) via a shared LegalPageLayout, with placeholder body copy, so the routes exist and are visually consistent with the rest of the site pending real legal copy and an actual design.

options.label: Build a minimal placeholder shell now (title + prose), reusing this frame's tokens, and backfill real copy/layout later
Block implementation until a dedicated Privacy Policy / Delivery Terms Figma design and final legal copy are supplied

open_questions.topic: Whether this story should build the entire footer or only the legal-links row
open_questions.detail: The two legal links only exist inside the full footer (node 6:136), which also contains FooterBrand, a Kitchen Hours column, and a Pizzeria Location column — none of which relate to legal pages. The footer does not exist at all yet in this repo (no footer component of any kind), so building just the legal row means shipping a footer that is missing its brand/hours/location content.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Scope this story narrowly: build only the minimal footer shell needed to host FooterLegalRow (copyright + the two legal links) at the bottom of the page, and leave FooterBrand/Kitchen-Hours/Pizzeria-Location columns to a separate 'site footer' story so this story's diff stays focused on its stated goal.

options.label: Build only a minimal footer shell + FooterLegalRow now; defer FooterBrand/hours/location columns to a separate footer story
Build the entire footer (6:136) as designed now, since the legal row's design only exists nested inside it

open_questions.topic: The supplied component catalogue says the project is greenfield, but it is not
open_questions.detail: This mapping task's catalogue states there are no existing UI components (apps/web/src/components/ui does not exist in this repo layout at all). In reality this repository already implements SiteHeader, PrimaryNav, NavLink, BrandLogo, and DeliveryIndicator under src/features/site (built for STORY-004, which mapped this exact same Figma frame). Treating this map as pure greenfield risks an implementer duplicating or diverging from that existing header/nav code.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Follow the mapping task's literal instruction and mark every component_map entry status as 'proposed_new' (no catalogue was supplied to override), but flag in notes on every header/hero-adjacent entry that a real implementation already exists at a specific repo path so a human doesn't rebuild it from scratch.

options.label: Follow the given empty catalogue literally: mark every component proposed_new as instructed, noting real existing paths only in free-text notes
Override the given catalogue with the repo's actual existing components and mark status=existing for nodes with a real implementation (SiteHeader, PrimaryNav, NavLink, BrandLogo, DeliveryIndicator)

open_questions.topic: URL paths for the two legal pages are not specified anywhere in the design
open_questions.detail: Figma only provides the visible link labels 'Privacy Policy' and 'Delivery Terms'; no href/URL is encoded in the frame data.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Use kebab-case route paths derived from the labels: /privacy-policy and /delivery-terms, added to src/features/site/routes.tsx alongside the existing '/' and '/menu' routes.

open_questions.topic: Footer legal links are styled identically to the (non-interactive) copyright text
open_questions.detail: Nodes 6:172 (copyright), 6:174 (Privacy Policy), and 6:175 (Delivery Terms) all share the exact same fill (60%-opacity white) and type style (Geist 400/12); the design draws no hover/underline/color state that would visually distinguish the links from plain text.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Render 6:174/6:175 as real anchor/RouterLink elements (since they must navigate somewhere) using the same visual style as drawn, and add only a browser-default focus outline for keyboard accessibility; no bespoke hover treatment is invented since none is drawn.

open_questions.topic: Header, hero, delivery-banner, featured-section, and story-section are mapped for completeness only
open_questions.detail: This story's scope is the footer legal links and their destination pages. The rest of the frame is included in this component_map only so the full page is accounted for, per this mapping task's instructions. Design judgement calls specific to those sections (responsive breakpoints, shared Button/SectionHeading variants, the duplicated 'Cart' affordance, etc.) were already raised as open questions in STORY-004's design-context.json at this same path and are not repeated here.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Do not re-derive or re-litigate STORY-004's open questions for out-of-scope sections in this story's review; only the legal-page-specific questions above are actionable for this story.
